clue.text: Not against roughing up an opponent

indicators.note: to rough something up is to knock it about, so the letters of the two words before are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone declares themselves not against giving a rival a going-over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughing up' rearranges the ten letters of NOT AGAINST.
explanation.definitionFit: An antagonist is an adversary, the person you are pitted against.

clue.text: When abroad we show common sense

definitions.text: When abroad we show common sense

parts.words: When abroad we show common sense
parts.note: reads as tourists behaving sensibly, but the French pronoun for 'we' is also the English informal word for gumption

explanation.walkthrough: The four-letter French word for 'we' is borrowed into British English (from Greek) as practical good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous, borrowed from Greek, is British informal for practical intelligence or gumption.

clue.text: Some British submarines set up and spring a trap

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means read upwards, so the hidden run is backwards
some of the following letters, a run hidden across two words

explanation.surface: Royal Navy submarines are positioned to catch an enemy unawares.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside BRITISH SUBMARINES, 'set up' reads upward: HSUBMA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To ambush is to lie in wait and attack by surprise.

clue.text: Ended series, having exceeded time allowed

parts.note: over means finished or ended
a run is a series, as a run of luck

explanation.surface: A broadcast series has finished, having gone past its slot.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to go on longer than scheduled; this is the past participle.

clue.text: Country rain storm

indicators.note: a storm whirls things around, so the letters of rain are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rainstorm sweeps across a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia.

clue.text: Crime of corrupt senator

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or altered, so the letters of senator are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dishonest politician is guilty of an offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason, betraying one's country, is a serious offence.

clue.text: Not a starter in the ocean race

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
a course is a race track or the run of a race

explanation.surface: A yachtsman not starting in an ocean race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a starter' looks like a racing entrant who drops out; it means the big dish after the first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The main dish comes after the starter, so it is not an appetiser.

clue.text: Jovial acknowledgment of a bad standard

parts.note: jolly means jovial and cheerful
roger is the radio word for message received

explanation.surface: A cheerful nod of approval for poor work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' is a flag; the bad flag is the pirates' skull and crossbones.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull-and-crossbones flag flown by pirates is a villain's banner.

clue.text: An overhead light

parts.note: reads like a ceiling lamp, but means the glowing ring painted above a saint's head

explanation.definitionFit: A saint's glowing ring floats above the head, literally a light overhead.

clue.text: Mixes drink to raise funds

definitions.note: the event is held for the purpose of raising money, so the phrase describes it

parts.note: mixes up, as a verb, means jumbles
ale is a drink, a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up a cocktail as a charity fundraiser.
explanation.walkthrough: A JUMBLE SALE is a British charity sale of donated second-hand goods, held to raise money.
explanation.definitionFit: A rummage sale of donated junk exists chiefly as a fundraising event for a church or school.

clue.text: An alto composition lacking an established key

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters of the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: An alto singer's new piece of music has no tonal centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges the letters of AN ALTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonal music is written without a tonic or home key.

clue.text: Have a cigarette and look happier

definitions.meaning: to put a match to a cigarette and start smoking
a face brightens when its owner cheers up

explanation.surface: A smoker's mood improves as soon as the cigarette is lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Igniting a smoke and a face brightening with pleasure share the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: A poor reason for limping?

definitions.meaning: read literally, the excuse a lame person has for hobbling

explanation.surface: A feeble justification offered by someone who is hobbling.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeble pretext is called lame, and a lame person's limp has its own reason.

clue.text: He won't get the sack if the bag's big enough

definitions.text: He won't get the sack if the bag's big enough

parts.words: He won't get the sack if the bag's big enough
parts.note: reads like a worker kept on if his sales are good, but the bag is the day's tally of shot birds on an estate

explanation.definitionFit: An estate employee rearing birds for shooting keeps his job when the shoot's tally is large.

clue.text: Courses for non-drivers?

parts.note: suggests driving lessons, but means the routes walkers use rather than motorists

explanation.definitionFit: Footways are routes for pedestrians, who do not drive.

clue.text: Sort of map to study on a journey

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
a tour is a journey

explanation.surface: Advice to read up on a map while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for 'study' is an old usage, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A contour map shows the height of land by lines joining points of equal elevation.

clue.text: Move stealthily like an American Indian, quietly

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A Native American scout moving silently.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to move slowly and quietly to avoid notice.

clue.text: Scot returns to service in Scotland

indicators.note: the Scottish name is read in the backward direction, as if turning back

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish first name
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A Scotsman comes back to serve in his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: NAIRN is a town on the Moray Firth in northern Scotland; the definition is just 'in Scotland', a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: The town lies on the Moray Firth in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: It takes me only an instant to write a short note

parts.note: taken as written
mo is short for moment, an instant

explanation.surface: A busy writer boasts that jotting a quick message takes no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is British informal for a moment, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorandum is a brief written message, often internal to an office.

clue.text: Boast about dress

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for dress is read backwards

parts.note: garb means clothing or dress

explanation.surface: Someone shows off about an outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag is to boast or talk big about yourself.

clue.text: Being the boss I interrupt the cook

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into something, so the letter goes inside the word for a cook

parts.note: a chef is a cook

explanation.surface: A boss asserts the right to butt in on the kitchen staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief is the head person, the one in charge.

clue.text: It may be smoked and eaten with butter

definitions.meaning: a pipe made from a hollowed-out maize core
maize on the ear, served buttered

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that can be smoked or eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of an ear of maize is made into pipes, and the whole ear is served hot with butter.

clue.text: Natural cover in the Garden of Eden?

definitions.text: Natural cover in the Garden of Eden?

parts.words: Natural cover in the Garden of Eden?
parts.note: suggests shade from trees, but means the plant-based clothing Adam and Eve made to hide their nakedness

explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Adam and Eve sewed leaves of this tree together to cover themselves.

clue.text: Snow shoe accepted by some backward Arctic people

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken in, so one piece goes inside the other
backward means the word some is written from its last letter to its first

parts.note: a ski is a long runner worn on the foot for travelling over snow

explanation.surface: Some backward Arctic folk take to snowshoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' reverses the word some; 'accepted by' then takes the snow shoe inside. The name is now often considered offensive; Inuit is preferred.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the indigenous inhabitants of the far north, such as the Inuit and Yupik.

clue.text: Initiator of enterprise needs one in support

indicators.note: in places the word for one inside the word for a support

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar, as of a bridge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A business founder needs someone to back them up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is the first to open up a new field or venture.

clue.text: Corrosive sort of acid from a unit rich in chemicals

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the words, the run lying inside them
the letters are taken from within the words, the run lying inside them

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about an acid found in a strong compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitric acid is a strongly corrosive mineral acid.

clue.text: Islander comes out of a trance

indicators.note: coming out of something means emerging changed, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone from an island wakes from a trance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes out of' rearranges TRANCE; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cretan is a native of Crete, the large Greek island.

clue.text: American leaving Euston for school

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so those letters go out of the station name

parts.note: US is short for American, of the United States

explanation.surface: An American traveller departs from Euston station heading to school.
explanation.walkthrough: Euston is a London railway station; ETON is the famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: Turn pale — possibly being guilty

indicators.note: to turn is to change round, so the letters of pale are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone goes white, perhaps because they did it.
explanation.walkthrough: In court a plea may be 'guilty'.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant's formal answer to a charge in court may be guilty or not guilty.

clue.text: Hardcastle is converted in religious places

indicators.note: to convert is to change form, so the letters of the name are rearranged; it puns on religious conversion

explanation.surface: A man named Hardcastle undergoes a religious conversion in churches.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathedrals are the principal churches of dioceses, places of worship.

clue.text: Stage favourite's come-back

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A star of the stage makes a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a stage in a process.

clue.text: Wholesome belief I can spread around

indicators.note: spreading something around scatters it, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A believer hopes to spread a healthy creed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beneficial does you good, as healthy food does.
